case_title: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Rakesh Mishra
statutory_provisions: Prevention of Corruption Act s.13(2), s.13(1)(d); IPC s.120B
trial_court_outcome: Framing of charges against three accused
high_court_outcome: Set aside the order of framing charges
offence_finally_established: Criminal conspiracy, illegal gratification, and misuse of authority
neutral_facts: The accused, including Rakesh Mishra, were involved in granting building and completion certificates to a hotel and club without proper approvals. The original building permission was granted to the applicant, and later a revised plan was submitted. The revised plan involved significant changes from the original plan, including increased built-up area for the hotel and decreased for the club. The accused granted the revision without approval from any committee and accepted honorary membership in the club. The prosecution alleged that these actions constituted illegal gratification and misuse of authority. The High Court set aside the order of framing charges, but the Supreme Court restored the order, finding sufficient material to make out a prima facie case against the accused.
